label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you for keeping my bag safe and calling the number on my lab manual. I am grateful that you made the effort to contact me instead of abandoning it.

I am writing about the black Jansport bag I left in the Oshodi-to-Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I came down at Ikotun. It contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses.

Sir, I am a first-year Biology student, and I urgently need these things for my BIO 101 practical on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. We will not be allowed into the practical without our dissecting kits, so getting the bag back is very important to my studies.

I respectfully appeal to you to reconsider the ₦40,000 you requested. I cannot afford it. I can manage ₦10,000 towards your transport and as a sincere thank-you for keeping my belongings safe. That is my entire allowance, and I cannot raise anything beyond it. I can give you the ₦10,000 when we meet and you return the bag.

I appreciated how politely you spoke to me during our first call. However, being told afterwards to pay ₦40,000 “or forget the bag” was worrying. These are my personal belongings and school materials, and I am asking that we arrange their return without making a payment I cannot afford a condition.

Please choose a convenient day and time before Wednesday for us to meet during daylight. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me. We could meet at Ikotun roundabout or, if easier to locate, outside the Ikotun Police Division gate—simply as a clear, public meeting point.

Thank you again for keeping the bag. Please reply to confirm whether this arrangement is acceptable and when we can meet.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
